Yes, two of the CAPAs trace back to the same cause, the INC-03 incubator door switch fault. The other three CAPAs don't share a cause with each other.

**CAPA-26-012 and CAPA-26-015**
- **CAPA-26-012** comes from DEV-26-011, an OQ test incident. During TC-OQ-INC-04, the INC-03 door-open alarm fired at 142 s against a limit of ≤ 60 s. The recorded root cause is "Door switch misaligned" (equipment component).
- **CAPA-26-015** comes from DEV-26-033, the PPQ26-02 harvest viability deviation. INC-03's door was found not fully latched on 11-Jun. The recorded root cause is "Operator did not confirm door latch per SOP-MFG-105" (human error), and the CAPA is operator retraining.
- Both deviations are linked to the same equipment, INC-03.

**Why the root causes are really one**
- CC-26-019 (replace and realign the INC-03 door switch) was opened 24-Feb-2026 and approved, but its status is "APPROVED - NOT IMPLEMENTED". CAPA-26-012 is still OPEN, with a due date of 31-Mar that has passed.
- So the faulty door switch was a known issue and was still unfixed when the June event happened. On 10-Jun the INC-03 events were a door-open alarm at 21:40 and a low-temperature alarm at 22:22. Both were acknowledged only at 07:50 the next morning.
- The June deviation was attributed to operator error, but the unrepaired door switch and its late or unreliable alarm is the likely upstream cause. Retraining alone (CAPA-26-015) wouldn't address it. CAPA-26-015 is also marked closed, but its effectiveness check is still PENDING.

- CAPA-26-008 is the FRZ-80-02 compressor failure.
- CAPA-26-016 is low CD3% at apheresis (donor variability).
- CAPA-26-019 is a supplier tubing-set weld defect.
- None of these links to INC-03 or to each other in the data.
